input:
Once the corrosion allowance has been added, the compressor wall thickness works out at 21 mm, a thickness for the corroded condition rather than for new plate. In other words, a wall that is measured at 21 mm in service is effectively at its design limit rather than comfortably above it. The same allowance basis was applied to the absorber in the preceding section, for essentially the same reason: the thickness that matters is the one remaining at the end of the inspection interval.

Turning to the gasket for the compressor discharge flange, the comparison between the two materials is based on temperature limit alone. The graphite laminate has the higher limit and the polytetrafluoroethylene gasket the lower one, and the compressor discharge temperature lies closer to the lower limit than the margin normally kept in a design of this kind. The preference is therefore for the graphite laminate, purely on the basis of temperature limit; sealing performance and cost do not form part of this particular comparison and are not decided at this stage.

The position differs for the lean solvent pump, whose discharge flange runs at a lower temperature on a different fluid, so the lower-rated gasket's limit is not approached. There the choice depends on considerations not yet weighed in this section, beginning with the effect of the pumped fluid on each material over an inspection interval.

The same allowance basis was applied to the absorber in the section before this one, and for the same reason: the thickness that matters is the one remaining at the end of the inspection interval.

The gasket choice for the compressor discharge flange turns on temperature limit alone. Of the two materials compared, the graphite laminate carries the higher limit and the polytetrafluoroethylene gasket the lower, and the discharge temperature of the compressor sits closer to the lower limit than the margin the design usually keeps. The preference is therefore for the graphite laminate, on temperature limit only; sealing performance and cost were not part of the comparison and are not decided here.

The comparison does not run the same way for the lean solvent pump, whose discharge flange sees a lower temperature and a different fluid, and where the lower-rated gasket's limit is not approached. There the choice falls back on grounds this section has not yet weighed, beginning with what the pumped fluid does to each material over an inspection interval.
